name: search_code
description: Search the project source with the most deterministic engine that fits the question. Default to engine="ast-grep": structural AST patterns with metavariables ($NAME, $$$ARGS) — use this whenever you are looking for a code *shape* rather than text, including plain symbol/name lookups. It works on this project's own Zig source too: sgconfig.yml registers a Zig grammar built by tools/grammars/build.sh, so patterns like "const $A = @import($B);" or "pub fn $N($$$A) $R { $$$B }" match real syntax and never a comment or a string. If it returns an error about the grammar, run tools/grammars/build.sh once. engine="semcode": semantic queries over an indexed C/C++/Rust tree (needs .semcode.db). engine="rg": ripgrep regex — last resort, only for plain text, file names, or patterns ast-grep cannot express as syntax. Prefer ast-grep over rg whenever the query could be phrased as a code structure. Input: {"engine": "rg" | "ast-grep" | "semcode", "query": "...", "path": "."}. Returns {"ok": bool, "code": int, "stdout": "...", "stderr": "..."}.
llm_description: Search project source. engine: "ast-grep" (default) — structural AST patterns with metavariables ($NAME, $$$ARGS); use for code shape or symbol lookups, works on this project's Zig via sgconfig.yml (run tools/grammars/build.sh if grammar error). "semcode" — semantic queries over indexed C/C++/Rust tree (needs .semcode.db). "rg" — ripgrep regex, last resort for plain text/filenames only. Input: {engine, query, path}. Returns {ok, code, stdout, stderr}.
